section_1.title: The Prerequisite: Slope as a Static Ratio
section_1.content: Before understanding the derivative, we must recall the slope of a line. A line has a constant rate of change (rise over run). Use a visual of a static staircase to represent this constant 'steepness'.
section_1.example: A squirrel climbing a straight wooden ramp at a constant incline.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Transforming the Curve into Micro-Lines
section_2.content: Introduce a smooth, curved path. Explain that a curve is not a single slope, but a collection of infinite tiny segments. Zoom in on a point on the curve until it looks like a straight line. This 'local linearity' is the heart of the derivative.
section_2.example: A drone pilot flying a curved path; at any split-second, the drone's instantaneous orientation defines a single straight-line vector.

section_3.title: The Process: The Limit of Secants
section_3.content: Visualize two points on a curve. As the distance between them shrinks to zero (the Limit), the secant line transforms into the tangent line. Use an animation showing the second point sliding toward the first until they merge.
section_3.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: the 'average velocity' over 10 seconds versus the 'instantaneous velocity' at exactly 3.0 seconds.

section_4.title: Interpretation: The Derivative as a Sensitivity Mapper
section_4.content: Reframe the derivative not just as a 'slope', but as a 'sensitivity machine'. If the input changes by a tiny amount, how much does the output transform? This emphasizes the derivative as a dynamic transformation factor.
section_4.example: A balloon expanding: as the radius increases, how rapidly does the surface area transform? The derivative links the input growth rate to the output growth rate.

section_5.title: Conclusion: The Dynamic Lens
section_5.content: Summarize the transformational view: Calculus turns 'change' into a 'snapshot'. We don't just measure values; we measure the 'potential to change' at every point along the path.
section_5.example: Summarizing the journey from the squirrel on the ramp (constant) to the drone on a curve (variable) as the shift from Algebra to Calculus.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Slope defines a constant rate of change.", "Rise over run creates static steepness.", "Straight lines have predictable, steady paths."]
        self.setup_layout("The Prerequisite: Slope as a Static Ratio", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual assets
        line = Line(start=[-1, -1, 0], end=[1, 1, 0], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(line, "C2", "D5")
        
        p1 = Dot(line.get_start(), color=RED)
        p2 = Dot(line.get_end(), color=RED)
        
        label_slope = MathTex(r"m = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(label_slope, "B3")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Create(line), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE), FadeIn(p1), FadeIn(p2), Write(label_slope), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
